name: The subject marker が
definition: が marks the subject of the predicate: ねこが います (there is a cat), せんせいが おしえます (the teacher teaches), あたま が いたいです (my head hurts). Many N5 patterns take が with their subject: the existence verbs います・あります, 〜が すきです・きらいです, 〜が わかります・はなせます, and weather verbs like あめが ふります. In questions that ask who or what did something, the question word takes が: だれが きましたか (who came?), なにが ありますか (what is there?). When a topic and a subject both appear, は frames what the sentence is about and が marks the subject inside that comment: きょうは てんきが いいです, ふゆは ゆきが ふります. Textbook formulas that reduce が to 'new information' and は to 'old information' are rough guides, not rules; this contrast is stated carefully pending human review. See the topic-wa concept for は.
form_rules: NOUN が PREDICATE: ねこが います; せんせいが おしえます
QUESTION-WORD が + verb when the question asks for the subject: だれが きましたか; なにが ありますか
TOPIC は ... SUBJECT が ...: ふゆは ゆきが ふります
が also marks the subject inside a noun-modifying clause: せんせいが おしえる ほん (the book the teacher teaches)
usage_rules: Particles are not dropped: say が even when the subject seems obvious
Do not swap は and が freely: when both appear, は sets the frame and が marks the subject inside it
Topic use of は is covered by the topic-wa concept; this concept covers only が and the が/は pairing

en-US: dropping が in existence sentences (*neko imasu)
using は after a question word when the question asks for the subject (*dare wa kimashita ka? for 'who came?')
treating 'が = new information, は = old information' as a fixed rule instead of a tendency

name: と: with someone, A and B (companion and list)
definition: と joins nouns. Companion use: NOUN と VERB means doing the verb together with X: きょうだいと なかよく します (I get along with my siblings). List-conjunction use: A と B means A and B: せんぱいと こうはいが きます (the senior and the junior come), しょうせつ と し を よみました (I read a novel and a poem). と is 'with' for companions and 'and' only for nouns; joining verbs or sentences uses the て-form, and means or instruments take で, not と. NOUN と NOUN (A and B): せんぱいと こうはいが きます
NOUN と の NOUN modifies a noun with a companion relation: ともだち と の きずな (the bond with a friend)
usage_rules: The と companion phrase comes before the verb it accompanies
List と joins nouns only; chain predicates with the て-form instead
Means and instruments take で; と marks companions and joined nouns

name: The quotation particle と (said/thought that …)
definition: と marks quoted content — the words someone said, thought, or asked. It follows the quoted words or a plain clause and attaches to speech verbs such as 言います, おもいます, ききます, かきます: こーちが 「じょうずに なった」と 言いました (the coach said 'you got better'); げんきだ と おもいます (I think I am well). The quoted part keeps its own tense and politeness; only the speech verb inflects. In writing the quote usually appears inside 「」, but the spoken cue is always と. This と is the same shape as the companion/conjunction と (see the companion-to concept); the existing verb.to-omou and youni-versus-to concepts cover fragments, this concept is the particle itself. Draft definition pending review.
form_rules: QUOTED WORDS or PLAIN CLAUSE + と + 言います/おもいます/ききます
the quoted clause may be polite or plain: 「わかりました」と 言いました
tense and politeness sit on the speech verb: 〜と言いました, 〜と思います
usage_rules: put と directly after the quoted content, before the speech verb
for opinions, 〜と おもいます takes the plain form of the quoted predicate (see verb.to-omou)
desired-state ように is not quotation (see youni-versus-to)

name: い-adjective inflection (〜くない, 〜かった, 〜くなかった)
definition: い-adjectives inflect themselves: they do not need a separate helper word to be negated or put in the past. Drop the final い and add the ending. Present affirmative おいしい; plain negation おいしく ない; polite negation おいしく ないです; past おいしかった (polite おいしかったです); past negation おいしく なかった (polite おいしく なかったです). The word いい is irregular across the whole paradigm: past よかった, negation よくない, past negation よくなかった (never いいかった or いいくない). な-adjectives follow a different pattern (きれいじゃない), so do not mix them (see adjectives.na-attributive). Draft definition pending review.
form_rules: stem + い = present: たかい (it is expensive)
stem + くない = plain negation; + くないです = polite negation: たかくない / たかくないです
stem + かった = past, + かったです polite: たかかった / たかかったです
stem + くなかった = past negation: たかくなかった / たかくなかったです
いい exception: past よかった, negation よくない, past negation よくなかった
usage_rules: negation and past live in the adjective ending; です only adds politeness (see politeness.register)
before a noun the dictionary form with い is used: たかい ほん (an expensive book)
〜くない alone is plain style; use 〜くないです with strangers and teachers

en-US: *たかいですかった or *おいしい for past (the ending must change: たかかった, おいしかったです)
*いいかったです or *いいかった for the past of いい (it is よかったです/よかった)
*おいしいくない by stacking forms (negation replaces the い: おいしくない)
applying い-adjective inflection to な-adjectives (*きれくなかった — use きれいじゃ なかった)
